questions.q: According to the textbook, what is required to produce an electromagnetic wave that propagates through space?
options: A stationary electric charge sitting at rest, producing a static field
An oscillating (vibrating) electric charge, such as a charged sphere oscillating up and down on a spring
A charge moving at constant velocity as a steady direct current
A constant magnetic field of sufficient strength
questions.explanation: The textbook states that to produce an electromagnetic wave which propagates through space, an oscillating (vibrating) electric charge is required. The oscillating charge forms an electric current that oscillates in magnitude and direction, inducing oscillating magnetic and electric fields that are self-perpetuating and radiate out through space.

questions.q: The textbook summary states that electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating charges. Which example does it give of such accelerating charges?
options: A battery driving a steady direct current down a wire
Electrons oscillating at high frequency in a radio antenna
A permanent magnet held next to a stationary conductor
Protons held fixed in the nucleus of an atom
questions.explanation: The summary states electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating charges; for example, electrons oscillating at high frequency in a radio antenna produce radio waves. These waves are of the same nature as light but have a lower frequency.

questions.q: In Maxwell's time a medium was assumed to be required for electric and magnetic fields. What was this supposed medium called, and what happened to it?
options: It was called the luminiferous aether, and it was directly observed in the laboratory
It was called the luminiferous aether, but it was never observed; an electromagnetic wave is instead an oscillating electromagnetic field
It was called the slinky medium, and electromagnetic waves are ripples within it
It was called the mechanical medium, and it is required for all waves including light
questions.explanation: The textbook explains that the supposed medium was called the luminiferous aether, but it was never observed. An electromagnetic wave is not a ripple in a slinky string or on the surface of water; instead it is an oscillating electromagnetic field that perpetuates itself.

questions.q: From memory: why does a constant direct current not produce an electromagnetic wave, while a changing current does?
keyPoints: Constant magnetic and electric fields will not produce an electromagnetic wave.
It is changing electric fields that produce changing magnetic fields (and vice versa).
A steady direct current gives an unchanging field, so nothing radiates; only a change radiates.
questions.explanation: The textbook answer is explicit: changing electric fields produce changing magnetic fields, but constant magnetic and electric fields will not produce an electromagnetic wave. If you recalled that 'constant fields do not radiate, only a change does', mark yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q: Calculate the speed of electromagnetic waves given the permittivity of free space is \(8.854 \times 10^{-12}\) and the permeability of free space is \(4\pi \times 10^{-7}\), using Maxwell's relation.
questions.given: \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\) C² s² kg⁻¹ m⁻³,  \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\) m kg C⁻²
working: This equals the speed of light, which led Maxwell to propose that light is an electromagnetic wave.
questions.explanation: Substituting the permittivity and permeability of free space into Maxwell's relation \(v = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}\) gives \(2.998 \times 10^{8}\) m s⁻¹, the speed of light. Because both constants are fixed properties of the vacuum, the speed is the same for every electromagnetic wave.

questions.q: Ultraviolet light has a wavelength of 300 nm (\(3 \times 10^{-7}\) m). Using the wave equation, find its frequency. Take the speed as \(3 \times 10^{8}\) m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Rearranging the wave equation \(c = f\lambda\) gives \(f = c/\lambda = 1 \times 10^{15}\) Hz. Since the speed in a vacuum is fixed at c, frequency and wavelength are inversely related: shorten the wavelength and the frequency rises in exact proportion.

questions.q: According to Faraday's law as described in the textbook, what does a changing magnetic field induce?
options: A static charge that begins and ends in a magnetic pole
An electric field around a loop; if there is no change in the magnetic field, there is no electric field
A constant magnetic flux that does not vary with time
A permanent separation of magnetic monopoles
questions.explanation: Faraday's law describes the electric field induced by a changing magnetic field; this electric field forms a loop rather than beginning and ending in a charge. The textbook stresses that if there is no change in the magnetic field, there is no electric field around the loop — changing magnetic fields induce electric fields.

questions.q: The textbook states 'the shorter the wavelength, the greater the energy the wave carries'. On this basis, which forms of electromagnetic radiation does it identify as NOT ionising?
options: Gamma rays and X-rays
Infra-red, microwaves and radio waves
Ultraviolet rays and visible light
X-rays and ultraviolet rays
questions.explanation: The textbook explains the shorter the wavelength, the greater the energy the wave carries, with gamma rays highly ionising. Ultraviolet is also ionising, but visible light is not, and infra-red, microwaves and radio waves are not ionising — they do not deliver enough energy to individual electrons to free them from atoms.

questions.q: From memory, state the self-propagation loop of an electromagnetic wave using the two named Maxwell laws (the 'FAME' hook).
keyPoints: A changing electric field, by the Ampère-Maxwell law, induces a changing magnetic field at right angles to it.
That changing magnetic field, by Faraday's law, induces a changing electric field.
The two fields continuously regenerate one another, so the disturbance propagates outward as a transverse wave needing no medium.
FAME: Faraday makes Electric, Ampère-Maxwell makes Magnetic.
questions.explanation: The mark-earning spine is: Ampère-Maxwell named, Faraday named, the phrase 'regenerate one another', and 'no medium required'. If you produced all four, grade yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q: Describe the production of an electromagnetic wave. (2 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: An electromagnetic wave is produced by an accelerating electric charge — for example, electrons oscillating in an antenna driven by an alternating current. The oscillating charge produces a changing electric field, which sets up the self-propagating wave.

criteria.descriptor: States the source is an accelerating (oscillating) electric charge — the word 'accelerating' is essential.
Gives the named example of electrons oscillating in an antenna driven by an alternating current.

questions.explanation: The non-negotiable word is 'accelerating': a charge moving at constant velocity radiates nothing. Writing only 'a moving charge' loses the mark.
